step1_analysis.description: This circuit is a translinear feedback loop used to generate bias voltages for a low-voltage rail-to-rail input stage. It sums the gate-source voltages of the transistors (XMQ, XMQ2, XMQ3) to equal VDD, thereby adjusting the output bias voltages (VQ, N3) to maintain a constant transconductance (gm) across the input common-mode range.

paper_reference.title: Constant-gm Constant-Slew-Rate High-Bandwidth Low-Voltage Rail-to-Rail CMOS Input Stage for VLSI Cell Libraries

power_consumption.description: Total DC power consumption of the bias circuit.

sky130_expected.calculation: I_total = Iref + I_XMQ1 + I_XMQ3 + I_XMI1. For Iref=10uA, V_GS,XMQ = 0.62V, V_GS,XMQ2 = 0.51V. The translinear loop forces V_GS,XMQ3 = VDD - V_GS,XMQ - V_GS,XMQ2 = 1.8 - 0.62 - 0.51 = 0.67V. This results in I_XMQ3 ≈ 87uA. Total current ≈ 194uA. Power = 1.8V * 194uA = 349uW.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Higher than the paper's 7uW because VDD=1.8V forces a large V_GS on XMQ3 in this translinear loop, increasing current. The paper likely used a lower VDD (e.g., 1.0V - 1.2V) where the loop operates in weak inversion.

v_vq_bias.description: Output bias voltage for NMOS tail current sources.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Gate voltage of the diode-connected NMOS carrying the loop-generated current.

v_n3_bias.description: Output bias voltage for PMOS tail current sources.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Gate voltage of the PMOS carrying the loop-generated current.

psrr_vq.description: Power Supply Rejection Ratio at the VQ bias node at 1kHz.

sky130_expected.calculation: Since the translinear loop equation is V_GS,XMQ3 = VDD - V_GS,XMQ - V_GS,XMQ2, any change in VDD directly changes V_GS,XMQ3, leading to poor PSRR.
sky130_expected.reasoning: The circuit is highly sensitive to VDD by design (it's a VDD-dependent translinear loop), so PSRR will be poor.

startup_time.description: Time for VQ to reach 90% of its steady-state value after VDD is applied.

sky130_expected.calculation: Determined by the parasitic capacitances at N3, N2, VQ and the transconductances of the loop transistors. tau = C/gm ~ 10ps. Startup should be very fast, limited by the VDD ramp.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Matches the 1ns/2ns transient times reported in the paper.

gm_variation.description: Variation of the transconductance over the full input common-mode range.

sky130_expected.calculation: Cannot be simulated with this netlist alone as it requires the N and P differential pairs.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Typical constant-gm stages achieve 5-10% variation. The paper reports values like 2.63% and 3.57% for optimized cases.

step3_testbench.description: Testbench to measure the DC operating point, power consumption, PSRR, and startup time of the constant-gm bias circuit.
step3_testbench.spice:
* Constant-gm Bias Circuit Testbench
.lib "${SKY130_PDK}" tt

.param W_xmq2=5u L_xmq2=0.5u
.param W_xmi2=5u L_xmi2=0.5u
.param W_xmi1=5u L_xmi1=0.5u
.param W_xmq3=5u L_xmq3=0.5u
.param W_xmq4=5u L_xmq4=0.5u
.param W_xmq1=5u L_xmq1=0.5u
.param W_xmq=5u L_xmq=0.5u

VVDD VDD 0 dc 1.8 ac 1 pulse(0 1.8 1n 1n 1n 10m 20m)
Iref VA 0 10u

XMQ2 N3 N2 0 0 sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xmq2} w={W_xmq2}
XMI2 VQ VQ 0 0 sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xmi2} w={W_xmi2}
XMI1 VQ N3 VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l={L_xmi1} w={W_xmi1}
XMQ3 VDD VA N2 0 sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xmq3} w={W_xmq3}
XMQ4 N2 VQ 0 0 sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xmq4} w={W_xmq4}
XMQ1 N3 VA VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l={L_xmq1} w={W_xmq1}
XMQ VA VA VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l={L_xmq} w={W_xmq}

.control
* DC Operating Point
op
let power = -i(VVDD) * 1.8
print power
print v(VA) v(VQ) v(N3) v(N2)

* AC Analysis for PSRR
ac dec 100 1 1G
let psrr_vq = vdb(VQ)
meas ac psrr_vq_1k find psrr_vq at=1k

* Transient Analysis for Startup Time
tran 10p 5n
meas tran startup_time trig v(VDD) val=0.9 rise=1 targ v(VQ) val=0.6 rise=1

quit
.endc
